note: No rule of the Central Bank of Samoa fixing an account number's length was read. ANZ Bank (Samoa), in its page and Quick Reference Guide on the Central Bank of Samoa's national payment system upgrade under the National Payment System Act 2014 (from 16 May 2023; read 2026-10-30, the guide dated 05/23), gives each receiving bank's account number format, the bank being named by its SWIFT code beside the number (replacing the ACH codes WS01 to WS04): ANZ Samoa seven digits, BSP's Samoa branch ten, National Bank of Samoa ten, Samoa Commercial Bank thirteen (prefix 101, a seven-digit base number and a suffix from 201-250, 001-050 or 301-350) or, for numbers introduced in 2019, ten (a two-digit prefix and an eight-digit base number); short National Bank and Samoa Commercial Bank numbers are padded with zeros at the front, ANZ's and BSP's not. So the number is written as seven to thirteen digits, drawn at seven, ANZ's own format, the bank the game's Samoa account is held at. Reading to check: the guide's column is headed 'minimum number of digits required'; ANZ's own numbers are given as the format XXXXXXX with no longer one named. No check digit is published, and the bank isn't coded inside the number.
